items.q: The initial investigation of kidney disease pairs USG abdomen and renal function tests with:
items.exp: Initial investigation: ultrasonography (USG) abdomen, renal function test (RFT) and urine analysis. (Book p748)

items.q: For protein estimation in the initial urine analysis, the preferred test is:
items.exp: Urine analysis: 24hr protein (preferred), albumin/creatinine, protein/creatinine. (Book p748)

items.q: The RFT arm of the initial investigation measures:
opts: S. urea, S. creatinine, S. Na+ and S. K+
S. urea, S. uric acid, S. Ca2+ and S. Mg2+
S. creatinine, S. albumin, S. Na+ and S. K+
S. urea, S. creatinine, S. ALT and S. AST
items.exp: RFT: S. urea, S. creatinine, S. Na+, S. K+. (Book p748)

items.q: On the USG approach, a kidney size below which value points toward chronic kidney disease?
items.exp: Look for: kidney size <8 cm. (Book p748)

items.q: Kidneys larger than 10 cm with loss of corticomedullary differentiation are classically seen with:
items.exp: >10 cm with loss of CMD with: DM, HIV, amyloidosis. (Book p748)

items.q: Enlarged (>10 cm) kidneys with loss of CMD are listed for all of the following EXCEPT:
items.exp: Loss of CMD with >10 cm kidneys: DM, HIV, amyloidosis; vesicoureteral reflux belongs to the asymmetric-kidney note. (Book p748)

items.q: Fill up: On the USG approach, seeing corticomedullary differentiation (CMD) places the patient in the ______ arm.
items.exp: CMD present → CKD; absent → non-CKD. (Book p748)

items.q: Match each normal-kidney USG structure with its echogenicity — 1) Cortex 2) Pyramids 3) Fat, calyx, sinus, vessels … A) Hyperechoic B) Isoechoic C) Hypoechoic
items.exp: Isoechoic: cortex; hypoechoic: pyramids; hyperechoic: fat, calyx, sinus, vessels. (Book p748)

items.q: Which statement about the USG approach is TRUE?
opts: USG abdomen is the most important investigation of the approach
Loss of CMD rules out chronic kidney disease
Kidneys of 8-10 cm always retain CMD
Absent CMD places the patient in the CKD arm
items.exp: USG abdomen (most important); CMD present → CKD, absent → non-CKD; 8-10 cm loss of CMD is itself a CKD clue. (Book p748)
